content.text: David Hume asked why we trust induction at all. The past does not logically guarantee the future.
Saying 'induction has worked so far' does not help. That argument is itself inductive, so it goes in a circle.

examples.title: Hume's challenge
lines: The sun has risen every day so far.
examples.note: Not valid: it is logically possible that it will not.

examples.title: A practical reply
lines: If nature is regular, induction will work.
If nature is not regular, no method will work.
examples.conclusion: So induction is our best bet either way.

question.prompt: Why is it circular to defend induction by saying it has worked before?
options: We do not know whether it worked
The defense is itself an inductive argument
question.hint: What kind of reasoning moves from 'it worked before' to 'it will work'?
question.explanation: Going from past success to future success is induction. Using induction to justify induction assumes what it tries to show.
